resources.scope: sampled owned process sums / whole-board GPU, not continuous CUDA allocator maxima

source_findings.finding: Windows MAX_PINNED_MEMORY=host RAM*0.40; registration budget, not task RSS/private/commit budget.
ensure_pin_budget checks allocation size plus max(RAM_CACHE_HEADROOM/2,2GiB) against system physical availability; does not read owned PrivateUsage or remaining system commit.
cache-classic sets cache_ram=0; execution RAM_PRESSURE node-boundary cache/pin pressure branch is not active for CLASSIC.

Dynamic pin allocation ensures physical and registration budgets then extends HostBuffer and calls cudaHostRegister; may create additional staging/host residency. Source does not enforce campaign private16GiB/RSS10GiB limits.
With fast_disk true and available VBAR signature, new pin allocation is skipped; signature None or nonfast/highRAM may attempt pins. Thus it is not necessarily full-model pinning.
HostBuffer max_grow_size derives from twice min(model size,registration cap); this is growth capacity, not evidence all bytes are committed immediately.
File-backed tensors can use native read_file_to_device path when no CPU destination; existing fast-disk behavior already avoids requiring a full host pin cache.

interpretation: Cannot prove enabling pin necessarily exceeds existing caps from static source; actual faulted subsets and native allocation behavior determine size
Native physical pressure can remain permissive while owned private exceeds16GiB or RSS exceeds10GiB; external controller may stop first
Current measured private headroom is only about1.81GiB and RSS headroom about4.92GiB;40percentof32GiB is about12.8GiB and is not an adequate task bound
Possible faster transfers are not measured here; defer rather than spend another GPU run on an unbounded switch
Do not add high_ram or disable_fast_disk to force pinning; those would change more behavior and pressure
limitations: Python/source and existing logs only; native DLL not rebuilt or allocation-traced
